question: Wave-WB's sizing correction: all 351 agreed serde `expecting` bodies' derived marker channel was `<end>` at tip — the CF_STR emission (compiled in, CF_STR=true) measurably did not fire. Why, and what does making it fire buy at both levels?
answer_root_cause: call_fwd_arg_admits' literal clause demanded an ADJUSTMENT-FREE `&str` literal — a shape built never mints temps for. Measured both directions (-Zdump-mir=built, probes/em2.rs): a literal passed to a `&str` param carries the reborrow pair [Deref(Builtin), Borrow(Ref(Not))] and built spells the TWO locals (`_4 = const "lit"; _3 = &(*_4)`) — the exact shape the plan's StrLit slot models; a literal passed to a `&'static str` param has NO adjustment and built FOLDS it (no locals, no markers). The clause therefore refused every real str-literal body and the whole CF_STR leg was dead code. The fix: StrLit REQUIRES the shared-reborrow pair; the adjustment-free literal stays refused (trust-ir says StrLit, HIR says fold — mask disagreement, fail closed, unchanged behavior).
method: Detached trust worktree at origin/main 7284cef657 (laneEM/wt), clean submodule d93b2fbb9, sysroot-v13. CONTROL sealed from the pristine tree; SUBJECT = control + (1) the corrected call_fwd_arg_admits literal clause, (2) the &str-literal PAIR admission in gate_derived_body (str_lit_pair_temps: pair-linked single-def / mentions==2 on BOTH locals, the storage-marker scalar gate and the Rvalue::Ref arm each extended pair-pinned), (3) the cf-lit-order SAT control (SatPerturb::CfLitOrder — swaps each pair's LIVE order through the sealed plan, so both sides of the marker law move together and only the frozen ORACLE can refuse).
